With consent of the parties, heard the matter finally.

2] This appeal under Section 173 of Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 has been preferred by the appellant/claimant for enhancement of compensation awarded by Motor Accidents Claims Tribunal, Distt Ratlam in Claim Case No. 47/2009 vide award dated 25.09.2010.

sentences.text: 3] Relevant facts in brief are that on 12.06.2009, appellant while going to Kharwakala at about 03:00 o'clock alongwith Ajju Kha on motorcycle bearing No. MP-13 ME 4523 and on arrival at Mandaval Road Napakheda, a tampo bearing No. MP07-T-0971 rashly and negligently NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-IND:3542 2 MA-3322-2010 driven by the respondent No.1 hit the appellant, as a result appellant has suffered grievous injuries including fracture of right leg, injuries on left hand and right hip.
He was admitted in M.S. Hospital, Ujjain from 12.06.2009 to 18.06.2009 wherein a rod was planted in his leg and plaster was made.
Though claim was made for Rs.7,00,000/-, the tribunal while awarding the amount of compensation has considered the entire Jaswantsingh vs Yusuf Khan And 2 Ors.

1 evidence placed on record and has awarded an amount of Rs.52,575/- with interest at the rate of 6%
per annum from the date 03.08.2009 under the heads; Rs. 14,575/- for medicines & investigations,
Rs. 2,000/- for transportation, Rs.3,000/- for special diet, Rs. 3,000/- for pain & suffering by the respondent Nos. 1 and 2.
However, directed the Insurance company to pay and recover from them.

4] Learned counsel for the appellant contends that the Claims Tribunal has committed an error in holding that there is no permanent disability of appellant- claimant caused due to the accident,
although the appellant had produced the documentary evidence which clearly shows that he had sustained grievous injuries including fracture of right leg, injuries on left hand and right hip.
Learned Tribunal assumed permanent disability of 10% in spite of 32.3% as per medical report (Ex-P/8) submitted by Dr. O.P. Gupta who has been examined as PW-2.
The Claims Tribunal has committed an error in awarding Rs.52,575/- towards transportation, special diet and attendance expenses looking to the nature of injuries sustained by the appellant.
The Claims Tribunal has awarded meager .
Hence, prayed for enhancement of proper compensation amount in favour of claimant.

5] On the other hand, learned counsel for Insurance Company as NEUTRAL CITATION NO.
2025:MPHC-IND:3542 3 MA-3322-2010 well as learned counsel appearing for respondent Nos. 1 &
2 have argued in support of the impugned Award and contended that Claims Tribunal has rightly awarded the compensation amount in the case, which does not call for any interference by this Court.
6] Heard learned counsel for the parties and perused the record.
7] After hearing learned counsel for the parties and going through the record, I find substance in the arguments advanced by the counsel for the appellant.
From the perusal of the record and as per para 16 of the impugned order, the appellant is having agriculture land and earning Rs.2 to 2.50 lakhs per annum.

Due to accident,
there has been some reduction in agriculture income.
Therefore, his income can be assumed to some extent.

8] On perusal of medical documents produced on behalf of appellant/claimant before the Claims Tribunal and looking to the injuries sustained by the appellant, especially the permanent disability certificate produced by doctor concerned, this Court thinks it appropriate to award the compensation by modifying to some extent.
The Claims Tribunal has assumed 10% permanent disability but future prospects have not been added in his income.

Hence, by adding future prospects, it should be Rs.3,750/- per month and therefore, for 12 months, it will be Rs.45,000/-
and after multiplier into 13, it becomes Rs.58,500/-.

Likewise, awarded amount in other heads is also required to be enhanced as follows :-
 Heads Amount  Medical Expenses : Rs.14,575/-
 Pain and suffering : Rs.5,000/-

] Thus, the just and proper amount of compensatio case is Rs. 95,075/- as against the Award of the Claims Tribunal of Rs.52,575/- Accordingly, the appellant/claimant is entitled to an additional sum of Rs.42,500/- over and above the amount,
which has been awarded by the Claims Tribunal.
10] In the result, this miscellaneous appeal is partly allowed, by enhancing the compensation amount by a sum of Rs.42,500/-.
The enhanced amount shall carry interest as fixed by the learned Claims Tribunal from the date of filing of claim petition till its realization.
The said amount be paid within a period of three months from the date of receipt of certified copy of this order.
Rest of conditions as imposed by learned Claims Tribunal shall remain intact.

11] If the enhanced amount of compensation is in excess to the valuation of appeal, the difference of the Court fee (if not already paid) shall be deposited by the appellant- claimant within a period of one month and proof thereof, shall be submitted before the Registry.
Thereafter, the Registry shall issue the certified copy of the order passed today.
